reason: Both open with an over-cautious fire-hazard stop that doesn't fit this case, where a jammed brushbar and a snapped belt is the likely cause and no engineer is needed. Conversation 1 at least names the likely cause (a belt snapping from a hair jam) and suggests checking the brushbar with the vacuum unplugged, which is the right first step. It does wrongly raise motor winding damage and insist on an engineer. Conversation 2 gives only the generic stop-and-engineer message, asks no questions, and offers no diagnosis or path to a belt replacement.
